title: Investigate allocator drift causing gradual GPU memory rise during continuous batching
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observe a slowly increasing GPU memory footprint in production Dedicated clusters serving continuous-batched requests with active KV cache usage. The growth is not an immediate leak at process exit, instead it manifests as a gradual rise in resident GPU memory over hours of sustained traffic and does not recover to baseline after traffic drops. Hypothesis space includes: cudaMallocAsync arena growth and delayed trimming, allocator fragmentation from many small allocations for KV cache entries, delayed frees due to event/stream synchronization, and host pinned buffer retention from batched IO paths.

Key observations so far:
- Memory graphs (metrics/grafana/runtime/gpu_memory_retention) show a staircase-like upward trend correlated with sustained high batching (>40ms target latency) periods. Memory plateaus overnight but at a higher baseline.
- nvprof/Nsight captures of a short trace show many small device allocations (~1-16KB) during KV cache evictions and batch assembly, and frequent cudaFreeAsync calls that are paired with cudaEventRecord on non-default streams.
- Enabling CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1 on local repro increases memory arena sizes more quickly than when disabled; turning it off reduces drift but increases tail latency.
- Periodic manual calls to cudaMemPoolTrim (via a test harness) reduce resident memory temporarily but allocation churn resumes growth.

Repro steps attempted:
1) Microbenchmark that continuously issues simulated chat requests with 4 tokens average and heavy cache churn (random prefix substitutions) using same batching codepath as runtime. Reproduces upward trend within 2–3 hours on a 80GB A100 node.
2) Run with environment variable MALLOC_TRACE on allocator wrappers to log allocations; logs show a large percentage of transient allocations during prefix concatenation and tokenizer staging that are ~32–128 bytes after compression.
3) Attach to running process and take cudaMemGetInfo snapshots every 5m; free memory declines steadily while total device memory stays constant.

Hypotheses and reasoning:
- Hypothesis A: cudaMallocAsync arenas are resizing and not trimmed because frees are processed on different streams, delaying pool trimming. Evidence: frequent cudaFreeAsync + event pairs and known CUDA behavior where pool retention is stream-aware.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache uses many small device allocations per cache entry; pooling granularity causes internal fragmentation (arenas holding many small free segments) and prevents returning to OS-level allocator. Evidence: profiler shows many small allocations; arena growth matches number of unique cache entries created.
- Hypothesis C: Continuous batching reuses a small set of streams and records events to track completion; missed event synchronization or long-lived outstanding events prevents actual free until garbage collection at end of epoch. Evidence: some events remain in pending state for >30s in traces during dropped requests.
- Hypothesis D: Host pinned memory and asynchronous memcpy staging for batching holds pages and causes CUDA to keep more device pinned allocations. Evidence: traces show pinned host allocations rising in parallel.

Immediate mitigation ideas (short-term):
- Implement conservative periodic pool trimming: call cudaMemPoolTrim during low-traffic windows (e.g., every 5–10 minutes) to bound arena size.
- Add a flag to runtime to disable cudaMallocAsync for the KV cache allocator and use a fallback pooling allocator tuned for many small allocations.
- Reduce the use of cudaFreeAsync + cross-stream event patterns in batch assembly; prefer freeing on same stream or explicitly synchronize small critical paths.
- Limit KV cache entry GPU-side allocation size by coalescing small values into pooled segments (i.e., compact several small cache entries into a slab per shard) to reduce fragmentation.

Longer-term / engineering work (next steps):
1) Add deterministic microbenchmark harness that reproduces drift reliably within <1 hour on CI-sized instance. Instrument with per-arena stats exported to Prometheus. (owner: Diego)
2) Add allocator telemetry: per-pool allocated_bytes, reserved_bytes, free_chunks_count, largest_free_chunk exported at 30s cadence. Integrate with runtime Console. (owner: Marcus)
3) Prototype KV cache compaction strategy that preallocates N-byte slabs per shard and allocates entries from slab subranges; measure fragmentation reduction. (owner: Priya)
4) Implement a configurable runtime knob to disable cudaMallocAsync for certain allocators and use a custom small-allocation pool when enabled. Expose via config and GKE nodepool rollout flag. (owner: Diego)
5) Explore using cudaMemPoolSetAttribute to set trimming policy or integrate cuMemPoolTrim with longer-lived pools; engage NVIDIA support if behavior depends on driver/CUDA version. (owner: Asha)

Acceptance criteria for fix:
- No steady upward trend in GPU resident memory during 24h continuous-batching soak at production traffic profile (target < 5% baseline drift).
- Memory trimming does not increase p99 latency by >5% for chat endpoints.
- New allocator telemetry shows reduced fragmentation metrics under the same workload.

Links / artifacts:
- Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/mem-leak-repro
- Grafana dash: https://grafana.redwood/c/runner/runtime/gpu-memory-retention
- PR with initial allocator logging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
- Spike doc for slab compaction idea: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUN/kv-cache-slab-compaction-spike

Notes on trade-offs:
- Disabling cudaMallocAsync may reduce drift but increases latency and fragmentation risk moving to host pinned buffers. Need to measure p50/p99 impact across model families.
- Aggressive trimming reduces memory but may reintroduce allocation overhead that hurts tail latency. We should parameterize trimming windows and only enable on lower-priority tenants.
- Slab compaction increases implementation complexity and may make eviction/serialization code more brittle; however it directly addresses fragmentation for small allocations.

Next actions (this ticket):
- Diego: complete the deterministic repro harness and add per-arena prom metrics (ETA 2025-02-20).
- Marcus: land allocator telemetry PR and dashboard panels (PR 2345 reviewer: Marcus) (ETA 2025-02-25).
- Asha: run experiments toggling CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC on/off across driver versions (11.8/12.2) and file results in spike doc (ETA 2025-03-01).
- Priya: prototype slab-backed KV cache allocator in a branch for benchmarking (ETA 2025-03-10).
